shared_core_indexes.access_mode: official publisher links; local representation not held

reuse_rule: Austria and Germany refer to the same library-level German source index. Do not copy EU files into either national pack or create filesystem symlinks.

external_only_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2023/2667 on digitalisation of the visa procedure
external_only_references.review_state: Official English EUR-Lex text and instrument identity reviewed on 2026-10-23; the German EUR-Lex route is recorded but its text was not independently checked. This is an amending act, not a consolidated Visa Code. Article 8(2) makes general application depend on the Commission decision under Article 7(1), while Article 8(3) lists earlier application dates. Verify the Commission decision and any Austrian notification before describing the EU Visa Application Platform as operational. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

external_only_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 simplifying requirements for certain public documents
external_only_references.review_state: The official English text and Article 2 scope were reviewed on 2026-10-23. It covers specified Member-State public documents, including marriage and parentage records; Article 2(3) excludes third-country public documents and Article 2(4) excludes recognition of the legal effects of another Member State's document. The German route is recorded but its text was not independently checked. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

external_only_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2023/2685 on digitalisation of the visa procedure
external_only_references.review_state: Official English text and instrument identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. This amending act changes the uniform visa format to a digital format, but Article 3 defers general application to a Commission implementing decision under Article 2(1), with a limited exception for Article 1 point 2 from 27 December 2023. Check the decision in the Official Journal before describing digital visas as operational. This is not a consolidated text of Regulation (EC) No 1683/95. The German route is recorded but its text was not independently checked. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

external_only_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2018/1240 establishing ETIAS
external_only_references.review_state: EUR-Lex identifies the current consolidated version dated 12 June 2026. Article 2(1)(c) covers visa-exempt third-country family members of Union citizens or equivalent free-movement beneficiaries who lack the specified residence card or permit; Article 2(2)(b)-(c) excludes qualifying cardholders. On 2026-10-23 the official ETIAS FAQ said the system was not operating and no applications were being collected; the Commission scheduled launch for Q4 2026 without an exact date. Recheck official operational status and the actual residence document before applying. The German route is recorded but its text was not independently checked. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

external_only_references.title: Lounes, C-165/16
external_only_references.review_state: Official InfoCuria judgment record reviewed on 2026-10-23: 14 November 2017, ECLI:EU:C:2017:862; language of the case: English. English-language Court record linked. Scope: Derived residence of a third-country family member where the mobile Union citizen acquired the host Member State's nationality while retaining the nationality of origin. The source remains external-only; no local copy, country-topic coverage, or country completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Ruiz Zambrano, C-34/09
external_only_references.review_state: Official InfoCuria judgment record reviewed on 2026-10-23: 8 March 2011, ECLI:EU:C:2011:124; language of the case: French. English-language Court record linked. Scope: Article 20 TFEU and the exceptional derived residence position where refusal would deprive a Union-citizen child of the genuine enjoyment of the substance of Union citizenship rights. The source remains external-only; no local copy, country-topic coverage, or country completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: SM (Child placed under Algerian kafala), C-129/18
external_only_references.review_state: Official InfoCuria judgment record reviewed on 2026-10-23: 26 March 2019, ECLI:EU:C:2019:248; language of the case: English. English-language Court record linked. Scope: A child under Algerian kafala is not a direct descendant under Directive 2004/38 Article 2(2)(c); the host Member State must facilitate entry and residence after an individual assessment under Article 3(2)(a). The source remains external-only; no local copy, country-topic coverage, or country completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Wojewoda Mazowiecki, C-713/23
external_only_references.review_state: Official InfoCuria judgment record reviewed on 2026-10-23: 25 November 2025, ECLI:EU:C:2025:917; language of the case: Polish. English-language Court record linked. Scope: Recognition and, where needed, transcription of a same-sex marriage lawfully concluded by Union citizens while exercising free movement, for return and family-life purposes. The source remains external-only; no local copy, country-topic coverage, or country completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Stolichna obshtina, rayon “Pancharevo” (V.M.A.), C-490/20
external_only_references.review_state: Official InfoCuria judgment record reviewed on 2026-10-23: 14 December 2021, ECLI:EU:C:2021:1008; language of the case: Bulgarian. English-language Court record linked. Scope: A Union-citizen child’s identity document and free-movement rights where the host Member State's birth certificate names two mothers; this is a movement/document holding, not general harmonisation of parentage law. The source remains external-only; no local copy, country-topic coverage, or country completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Mirin, C-4/23
external_only_references.review_state: Official InfoCuria judgment record reviewed on 2026-10-23: 4 October 2024, ECLI:EU:C:2024:845; language of the case: Romanian. English-language Court record linked. Scope: Recognition of a Union citizen's first-name and gender-identity change lawfully obtained in another Member State while exercising free movement; it does not establish a general civil-status recognition rule. The source remains external-only; no local copy, country-topic coverage, or country completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Chavez-Vilchez and Others, C-133/15
external_only_references.review_state: Official InfoCuria judgment record reviewed on 2026-10-23: 10 May 2017, ECLI:EU:C:2017:354; language of the case: Dutch. English-language Court record linked. Scope: Assessment under Article 20 TFEU of a third-country parent’s derived residence claim, including the child's dependency, best interests and family-life circumstances; parentage alone does not decide the claim. The source remains external-only; no local copy, country-topic coverage, or country completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 (Brussels IIb) on jurisdiction, recognition and enforcement in matrimonial matters and parental responsibility, and on international child abduction
external_only_references.review_state: Official EUR-Lex record and source identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. EUR-Lex current consolidated text displayed as 2 July 2019; no later consolidation was listed in the record reviewed on 23 October 2026. Scope: Jurisdiction, recognition and enforcement for covered matrimonial and parental-responsibility decisions, and international child abduction. It excludes adoption decisions and does not establish parentage. Limitations: Check the applicable case-date, national procedural implementation, and any later act-specific amendments before relying on a provision. External-only reference; no local copy or country-topic coverage/completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2022/922 on the Schengen evaluation and monitoring mechanism
external_only_references.review_state: Official EUR-Lex record and source identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. Official Journal act published 15 June 2022; in force and applicable from 1 October 2022; EUR-Lex displayed no consolidated version on 23 October 2026. Scope: Peer evaluation and monitoring of application of the Schengen acquis, including visas, external borders, return, information systems, agency and private-service activities, and fundamental-rights safeguards. Limitations: This is an oversight/evaluation mechanism, not an individual complaint or appeal procedure; evaluation reports may be restricted. External-only reference; no local copy or country-topic coverage/completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2019/1896 establishing the European Border and Coast Guard
external_only_references.review_state: Official EUR-Lex record and source identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. Latest consolidated version listed by EUR-Lex on 23 October 2026, dated 31 December 2023; the record includes the 2021/1134 amendment. Scope: European Border and Coast Guard/Frontex mandate, joint operations, standing corps, fundamental-rights oversight and complaints, and Member-State responsibilities. Limitations: This does not set individual visa or residence-card eligibility rules. Review related implementing measures and national responsibilities for the issue at hand. External-only reference; no local copy or country-topic coverage/completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2019/817 on interoperability of EU information systems in the borders and visa fields
external_only_references.review_state: Official EUR-Lex record and source identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. Current EUR-Lex consolidated version dated 12 June 2026; record last reviewed by EUR-Lex on 28 August 2026. Scope: Interoperability of border and visa information systems, including identity matching, search, data access, correction, erasure and oversight safeguards. Limitations: System components have staged operational dates set by separate implementing decisions; do not infer a component's operational status from the consolidated regulation alone. External-only reference; no local copy or country-topic coverage/completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2019/818 on interoperability of EU information systems for police/judicial cooperation, asylum and migration
external_only_references.review_state: Official EUR-Lex record and source identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. Current EUR-Lex consolidated version dated 12 June 2026; record states that version is in force. Scope: Interoperability for police and judicial cooperation, asylum and migration, including data-access and data-protection rules. Limitations: System components have staged operational dates set by separate implementing decisions; check the relevant component, purpose and national authority before relying on it. External-only reference; no local copy or country-topic coverage/completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2025/13 on advance passenger information for law-enforcement purposes
external_only_references.review_state: Official EUR-Lex record and source identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. EUR-Lex current consolidated version dated 8 January 2025, corrected by Corrigendum OJ L 90502 of 17 June 2025. Scope: Collection and router transfer of API and other PNR data for prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorism and serious crime on extra-EU and selected intra-EU flights. Limitations: This is distinct from Regulation (EU) 2025/12 on border-control API. Consult the corrigendum, commencement provisions, and Member-State intra-EU flight notifications before applying. External-only reference; no local copy or country-topic coverage/completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Council Directive 2001/51/EC on carrier obligations and sanctions under Article 26 of the Schengen Convention
external_only_references.review_state: Official EUR-Lex record and source identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. Original Official Journal text, 28 June 2001. EUR-Lex displayed no consolidated-text link in the record checked on 23 October 2026; later transposition/currentness was not determined. Scope: Carrier return duties and financial penalties related to transporting third-country nationals without required travel documents; the Directive excludes international-protection cases from its financial-penalty rule. Limitations: National transposition and application must be checked separately; this is not a general entry-eligibility rule. External-only reference; no local copy or country-topic coverage/completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961)
external_only_references.review_state: Official UN Treaty Collection record inspected on 2026-10-23. It identifies the Convention as concluded at Vienna on 18 April 1961 and in force from 24 April 1964; the linked status page states its data were current as at 22 October 2026 and links the certified true copy (UNTS vol. 500, p. 95). Check the specific states' participation, declarations/reservations, and relevant diplomatic status before applying. This external link does not establish country coverage or a local text acceptance.
external_only_references.version_note: UN Treaty Collection record; no consolidated text version applies.

external_only_references.title: Vienna Convention on Consular Relations (1963)
external_only_references.review_state: Official UN Treaty Collection record inspected on 2026-10-23. Check the relevant states' participation, declarations/reservations, and the scope of any Article 36 issue before applying. external_only_references.title: Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention)
external_only_references.review_state: Official HCCH text inspected on 2026-10-23. Article 1 covers specified public documents for use in another contracting state and excludes documents executed by diplomatic or consular agents and administrative documents dealing directly with commercial or customs operations. The separate status table distinguishes contracting parties from entry into force for each party and lists declarations. Check the actual issuing and receiving states, effective dates, and any relevant declarations. Apostille coverage and document authenticity are not established by this link alone; no country-specific determination or local text acceptance is implied.
external_only_references.version_note: Official HCCH Convention text; associated status table last updated 30 June 2026.

external_only_references.title: Convention of 29 May 1993 on Protection of Children and Co-operation in Respect of Intercountry Adoption
external_only_references.review_state: Official HCCH text inspected on 2026-10-23. It applies to intercountry adoptions that establish a permanent parent-child relationship and meet the Convention's conditions; recognition depends on Convention procedures, including the required certification, rather than adoption status alone. Use the separate HCCH status record to check both states, effective dates for the relationship, acceptance of accessions, and declarations. This reference does not decide an individual adoption's recognition or imply a country-specific determination or local text acceptance.
external_only_references.version_note: Official HCCH Convention text; party and relationship status is maintained separately in the HCCH status table.

external_only_references.title: HCCH status table: Convention of 29 May 1993 on Intercountry Adoption
external_only_references.review_state: The table distinguishes contracting parties from entry into force, and records state-specific dates, declarations, and acceptance of accessions. Check both relevant states and the effective relationship date for a particular adoption. Table inspection establishes no case-specific applicability or country completion.
external_only_references.version_note: Official HCCH status table; last updated 17 June 2025.

external_only_references.title: Convention of 19 October 1996 on Jurisdiction, Applicable Law, Recognition, Enforcement and Co-operation in Respect of Parental Responsibility and Measures for the Protection of Children
external_only_references.review_state: Official HCCH text inspected on 2026-10-23. It addresses jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition/enforcement, and co-operation concerning parental responsibility and child-protection measures; it is not an intercountry-adoption recognition convention. The separate status table distinguishes party status from entry into force and lists state-specific declarations. Check the states, dates, and measure at issue. No country-specific determination, adoption coverage, or local text acceptance is implied.
external_only_references.version_note: Official HCCH Convention text; associated status table last updated 18 September 2025.
